analysis:
Both units are base-side text of docs/developer/build.md (lines 1-934 shown). No patch hunks or head text were supplied, so the actual change is not visible and cannot be diffed against the threat model. I found no concrete regression to cite. The base content is documentation only. It describes build, CI and release flow, including these security-relevant statements the next pass should check against any head change:
- Line 257: release publication registers the exact signed build via scoped POST /v1/releases; no manual approval or per-release hardware qualification (A-005, A-011, A-017, T-054).
- Lines 259-263: secret-bearing release jobs accept only verified signed tags or trusted master, and CI establishes official identity, not runtime Apple success (TB-011).
- Lines 334-337: signing and publication jobs retain approvals, credential scopes and same-run artifact checks.
- Lines 397-398: caches hold only unsigned build products, never signing keys or notarized bundles.
- Lines 33-35: the E2E testbed replaces Apple attestation only in the testbed and does not disable the production cohort gate.
- Lines 69-79: component CI path detection uses a local NUL-delimited Git diff; docs-only changes skip component jobs, but Release Integrity and Docs Lint stay unconditional.
- Lines 271-289: the Bedrock threat-review workflow uses an organization-membership read token and hash-locked dependencies.
If the head diff weakens any of these claims, for example by removing the signed-tag or approval requirement, caching signing material, or letting E2E bypass cohort or attestation gates in production, it would warrant review. Coverage limit: the unseen diff, the referenced scripts and workflows, and other files in the PR were not examined.
